implemented: The retained create-intent outer cgroup identity is passed into _readback and checked before native PID discovery.

Only outer/host/sandbox owned cgroups are inventoried. Unexpected descendant directories, symlinks, malformed/duplicate PIDs, more than128 unique PIDs, nonempty outer domain or inode changes reject the readback.
Sentry state.pid must be in the owned inventory and have argv0 runsc-sandbox. Exactly one Gofer has argv0 runsc-gofer. Both require exact final job ID and exact retained runsc-state --root flag.

Each proc-directory FD is anchored to the opened process. PID/starttime are parsed before and after; cmdline/cgroup/limits/executable inode stamps are rechecked through that same directory FD. Missing or changed identity is an error.

Sentry executable identity must equal the verified runtime manifest gvisor-bin/gvisor_sentry; Gofer must equal verified runsc. File hashes, owner/mode/nlink and inode stamps are checked using the existing trusted runtime verifier.

Both native actors must report exactly one canonical Max open files row with soft=hard4096. Missing, unlimited, duplicate or different values reject before start. Requirement fields independently require native4096 and analysis256.
Core process observations repeat after discovery/runtime hashing; complete owned-cgroup inventory and directory identities must match again. Lease, deadline and watchdog remain current throughout.

Bounded raw limits/stat/cgroup/argv, SHA256 command identity, role executable identity and parsed limits are retained under enforcement_verified.readback.native_processes. Whole serialized enforcement payload must fit48KiB, below the durable journal64KiB cap.
Native verification failure follows existing whole-cgroup cleanup/watchdog path, emits no output, does not finish the uncertain job, and never grants C22 release or dispatch.
important_qualifications: Temporary files and mocks model procfs/cgroups on macOS; they do not establish actual Linux procfd semantics, installed native4096, sidecar access, or runtime scientific compatibility.

A transient unrelated native helper exiting during exact inventory comparison can conservatively reject a valid job. Such a failure must be preserved and diagnosed; it cannot authorize execution or release.
Native limit observations are pre-start snapshots; they are not a claim about continuous FD usage maxima.
Actual reruns must retain the prior native256/numerical failure evidence, verify guest256 and all other readbacks, rerun NumPy-first numerical fixtures and compare repeated results.
scope: Operator-only Linux native FD enforcement readback preparation; no real procfs/runtime/cloud/analysis execution in these checks.
